description:
FILED s473t6d member 4 (Opus, 2026-09-20, finished s493).  PRE-EXISTING: measured
IDENTICAL on the batch tree and on a `git archive 268d7e00` extraction.

t/re/pat.t:416-441 is

    my %ans = ( 'ax13876y25677lbc' => 1, 'ax13876y25677mcb' => 0, ... );   # 8 keys
    for (keys %ans) {
        my $message = "20000 nodes, const-len '$_'";
        ok !(...), $message;
        $message = "20000 nodes, var-len '$_'";
        ok !(...), $message;
    }

`keys %ans` is HASH ORDER, and perl randomises it per process.  The perl oracle
and the PCL side are separate processes with separate hash seeds, so the 16 rows
appear under different NUMBERS on the two sides and the runner's description
pairing manufactures `(missing)` / `*extra*` pairs that differ every run.

MEASURED (s493, `--jobs 1 --timeout 180`, one file per invocation):

    tree  re/pat.t  233/136  DIFF   ROW DIFF 28 NEW / 32 FIXED
    base  re/pat.t  233/136  DIFF   ROW DIFF 28 NEW / 32 FIXED    (268d7e00 extraction)

and the two faillogs are 523 rows each, differing in exactly 10 rows, ALL of them
`20000 nodes, const-len '<random>'` / `var-len '<random>'`.  Logs:
scratch/s473t6d/ab/{tree,base}-pat.log, fl-{tree,base}-pat/.

THE FIX is one of:
 (a) register the file `*rows-unstable*` in baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv the way
     op/inc.t and re/pat_advanced.t are (#1082) -- but that opts the WHOLE file
     (523 rows) out of the row check, which is a lot to give up; or
 (b) normalise the rowkey for this shape, e.g. have PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc fold
     `20000 nodes, <kind> '<any>'` to a single key -- a per-file hack; or
 (c) better: make the row-pairing use the PERL side's own ordering for rows the
     two sides agree exist, so a permutation is not a divergence.
Not scheduled here; the round only had to say whether the churn was its own.


=== RE-MEASURED s494 (Fable), after #1966 removed the phantom rows around it ===
re/pat.t alone now reads 5 NEW / 7 FIXED, and the members CHANGE BETWEEN RUNS (run2: `20000 nodes, const-len 'ax13876y25677y21378y21378kbc'` + `Negative lookbehind`; run3: the `(?il), utf8=0, locale=C.UTF-8, char=46` family + the `...kcb` spelling as FIXED) -- so this task owns ALL of re/pat.t`s residual noise: descriptions built from hash order / per-run data.  Logs ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/c1966/run2.log, run3.log.

MEASURED AGAIN s492b (2026-09-21): after that batch's re/pat.t rows were re-spelled
(`--bless-fails` for that file alone), the IRREDUCIBLE churn is FOUR rows, and they are not
hash order -- they are a RANDOMISED test string: `20000 nodes, const-len
'ax13876y25677y21378y21378kbc'` one run, `...y21378zbc'` the next (plus the two `*extra*`
twins).  Same family, same consequence (every companion run over re/pat.t reads 4 NEW / 4 FIXED
that are not regressions), and the same fix applies: register the file *rows-unstable*.  See also
#2032, which measures two more files of this shape (re/charset.t, re/regexp_unicode_prop.t).
subject: re/pat.t: 16 blessed companion rows carry HASH-ORDER descriptions, so every run reports ~28 NEW / ~32 FIXED that are not regressions
